name: D. K. Wade
role: Manager of the LeMoyne Cattle Co. on Tepee bottom
bio: D. K. Wade made his home on Tepee bottom in 1884, where his wife and daughters joined him from Pittsburgh. As manager of the LeMoyne Cattle Company, he drove its first 500 high-grade heifers overland from Glendive to the Tepee bottom range in July 1884, graded a new road out of the bottom that December, and built a 200-acre pasture in early 1885, when the paper called him "Deacon Wade." In October 1885 he read the burial service at a ranch funeral, and in April 1886 he put a resolution into the by-laws of the Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' Association. In the fall of 1886 he and his sister went to Santa Barbara, California, for the winter.
